_title: F-1-like kerolox booster: two-pass jacket and turbine exhaust film
_comment: A 6.77 MN LOX/RP-1 first-stage engine at 7 MPa, MR 2.27 and area ratio 16, cooled in the arrangement of the F-1: a two-pass jacket (architecture C) to an area ratio of ten, fed at the injector end with 70 percent of the fuel and the rest bypassed to the injector, and the gas generator's turbine exhaust laid as a film over the extension from ten to the exit. The jacket is 90 down and 90 up circular Inconel 718 channels on a 0.5 mm wall, alternating around the circumference and turning in a ring at the aft end. 470 kg/s of n-dodecane, the RP-1 surrogate the property backend carries, enters at 290 K and 13.8 MPa, leaves at 354 K and spends 1.48 MPa over both passes. The coking ceiling of 560 K on the coolant-side wall binds, not the metal: the metal peaks at 725 K against a 900 K limit. A carbon layer of 60 micrometers at 0.2 W/m-K stands in for the soot a kerosene engine lays on its own wall, and its surface runs at 2830 K. The value is assumed, not measured, and the jacket depends on it. With no layer, holding the coolant-side wall at the coking ceiling needs channels too small for the flow, and the coolant runs out of pressure; a 20 micrometer layer closes the jacket for 2.6 MPa with the metal at 894 K, and this 60 micrometer layer for 1.48 MPa at 724 K. The F-1's tube count doubles from 178 to 356 at an area ratio of 3. This example holds 90 per pass, 180 around the wall, because a channel split is not built inside a multi-pass jacket. The gas generator at a mixture ratio of 0.416 and 6.65 MPa reads 1252 K at equilibrium, with 35 percent of its mass as graphite. A real fuel-rich generator does not reach that equilibrium, and the F-1's ran at about 1063 K, so the exhaust temperature here is overstated. The turbine takes 736 kJ/kg at a pressure ratio of 16.4 and an efficiency of 0.6, and its 75.7 kg/s leaves at 991 K and 405 kPa into a 100 mm slot at the joint. Under that film the C103 shell peaks at 1240 K, 433 K inside its limit, against a recovery temperature of 3205 to 3243 K. C103 stands in for the F-1's own extension shell, because the solver's shell materials are the hot-structure entries of the materials store. Counting the exhaust as flow beside the chamber and its thrust kept apart from the core, the engine delivers 306.4 s at its design back pressure (309.5 s if the film mixes fully). Where C is viable: large tube-wall boosters, which keep both manifolds forward of the gimbal. Heritage: the F-1, which ran alternating tubes down and back with 70 percent of its fuel.
